plan: This auction structure mirrors a second-price sealed-bid auction: the winner pays the second-highest bid (the clock price when the second-to-last bidder exits). In such mechanisms, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy - it maximizes expected profit regardless of others' bids. Bidding higher than value risks winning at a loss; bidding lower reduces win probability without improving price paid. Therefore, I will bid exactly my value of $26.

This auction structure is equivalent to a second-price sealed-bid auction: the winner pays the second-highest bid, and my own bid only determines when I exit, not what I pay if I win. Therefore, bidding my true value ($31) is the dominant strategy—it maximizes my expected profit regardless of others' bids. Bidding higher risks winning at a price above my value; bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities.

This is effectively a second-price sealed-bid auction (the winner pays the second-highest bid). In such auctions, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy—it maximizes expected profit regardless of others' bids. Bidding higher risks overpaying if I win with a low value; bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. With my value at $24, I should bid exactly $24 to ensure optimal outcomes in this one-shot game.
